concept.name: Money flow index
concept.definition: Gene Quong and Avrum Soudack's volume-weighted momentum oscillator: an RSI-style 0-100 calculation applied to typical-price money flows, so both the direction and the volume of each bar feed the reading.
concept.intuition: It is RSI with volume mixed in - an overbought reading requires not just rising prices but rising prices backed by rising dollar volume.
concept.mechanics: Typical price = (H+L+C)/3; raw money flow = typical price x volume, classified positive or negative by the change in typical price; MFI = 100 - 100/(1 + positive sum / negative sum) over 14 periods. Conventional overbought above 80 (truly extreme above 90), oversold below 20 (below 10).
concept.formula: MFI = 100 - 100/(1 + MoneyRatio); MoneyRatio = sum(PositiveMF, 14) / sum(NegativeMF, 14); RawMF = TypicalPrice x Volume; TP = (H+L+C)/3.
concept.failure_modes: In strong trends it pins above 80 or below 20 while price continues; volume spikes (expiry days, index rebalancing) distort it without any change in sentiment.
concept.misconceptions: MFI overbought is not a sell signal - the creators recommended the stricter 90/10 levels precisely because 80/20 fires too often in trends; and MFI is not interchangeable with RSI, since volume can make them diverge.
concept.example: If 14-day positive money flow is 120M and negative is 60M, the ratio is 2 and MFI = 100 - 100/3 ~ 66.7.
